title: An Open-Ended Benchmark and Formal Framework for Adjuvant Research with MLLM
claim: The benchmark spans three complementary data formats, each shown by a concrete example: open-ended Q&A, hallucination rejection, and formal descriptions.
layout: 3 panels: two stacked left, one tall right; color-coded boxes
description: A figure made of three colored text boxes, each holding a sample from one data type in the benchmark. Panel (a), top left, has a yellow background with blue monospace text. It shows an open-ended Q&A case on clonal expression of antigen receptors, with Question, Reasoning Process and Answer fields. Panel (b), bottom left, has a green background with brown text. It shows a hallucination case about mosaic RBD nanoparticles, with the same fields plus a 'Reason for Error' field. Panel (c), on the right, has a light blue background with red text. It shows an Adjuvant Formal Language case, a list of symbolic definitions such as Ag_1, Adj_1, Struc_1 and Form()/Mix() compositions, followed by a Natural language Text paragraph. Each panel has a bold caption below it. The eye goes first to the colored boxes and the bold field labels.
caption: Three Types of Data Display in Adjuvant Benchmark
abstract: Adjuvants play a critical role in modulating immune responses and are central to the development of vaccines and immunotherapies. Yet progress in this field is constrained by data scarcity and incomplete understanding of mechanisms of action, which limit the transition from experience-based design to AI-driven approaches. To address these challenges, we present the first benchmark dedicated to adjuvants, constructed in an open-ended Q&A format and annotated by domain experts. The benchmark comprises 1,294 Q&A pairs and 1,364 formal descriptions, providing a resource for evaluating general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and for developing domain-specific systems. We systematically assess 11 closed-source and 18 open-source MLLMs across dimensions including domain-specific Q&A, hallucination rejection, data generation, and instruction following. Results indicate that OpenAI-o1 (STS = 0.7495, LLM Score = 7.7) and DeepSeek-R1 (STS = 0.7415, LLM Score = 7.7) achieved the strongest performance among closed- and open-source models, respectively. In addition, we introduce a formal description framework for representing adjuvant design principles and immune mechanisms as structured abstractions, which can serve as building blocks for future domain-specialized MLLMs. Overall, this work provides a first step toward systematically integrating MLLMs into adjuvant research by offering a dedicated benchmark, comparative evaluation of existing models, and a formal foundation for future development. Data and code will be released at https://github.com/banjiuyufen/Adjuvant-Benchmark.
